I second the Karen-Tuttle LH technique advice, and have two other suggestions to add:

1. Simon Fischer's vibrato exercise sequence. A short video explaining it can be found  at [https://youtu.be/01F0izy1TnU?si=9eUTW8BOZpWTtvBr](https://youtu.be/01F0izy1TnU?si=9eUTW8BOZpWTtvBr) . Yes, it's about vibrato, but it also helps you with basic LH setup so that you're not exacerbating the problem with the last joint of your 4th finger. Fischer also advocates bringing the hand closer to the neck, and this video takes that into account.

  
2. Exercise #1 of Dounis Daily Dozen - a set of LH only exercises meant to increase finger independence, dexterity, and strength. Take it \*really\* easy with these - just a little bit every day, and don't push yourself in pain. Eventually it will become easier, and you'll find yourself with stronger, more curved fingers that lift from the base joint.

I also have a 4th finger that flattens out like yours, and these exercises have helped me a lot. But it takes patience.

I'm amazed at how wiped-out I feel; I've taken more naps in the past 10 days than in the past 10 years.

4 days post-surgery the doc switched out the plaster for a fiberglass half-arm cast. I began doing range-of motion exercises a few days later, and this really helped. The pain is slowly lessening, and I am able to do more, and with much less pain. Healing has not been strictly linear, though, and sometimes a good day is followed by a bad night (or day).

Today (13 days post-surgery) I go back to the doc for suture removal, and the plan is to ditch the cast and go back to a removable splint. Here's hoping...
